subject: Staged upgrade: version curation, maintenance window proposal & reversion plan
messages:
From: priyom_das <priyom@redwood.ai>
To: sylvia@novusbank.com, ops-team@novusbank.com
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, jonas_weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Staged upgrade: version curation, maintenance window proposal & reversion plan

Hi Sylvia / Novus ops team,

Thanks for the time yesterday. Attached is a compact proposal for the private cluster upgrade we discussed — focused on minimizing impact while keeping a fast reversion path if we see regressions. High level:

- Goal: move from model runtime v3.1.2 -> v3.2.0 (security and perf fixes) for the private VPC deployment on 10/19-10/20.
- Request: a 90-minute maintenance window per regional pod (suggested windows below).
- Safety: staggered canary -> widen -> full rollout with automated snapshot-based reversion and traffic-steering quiesce.

Key asks from Novus: approval of the windows below, a point-of-contact on the ops bridge for each pod, and sign-off on the rollback SLA in the attached maintenance_scope_summary.pdf. I included an initial compatibility matrix (initial_compat_matrix.xlsx) that maps model binaries, runtime flags, and known network firewall rules that need exception for warm KV pre-warm.

Proposed staging timeline (Pacific):
- Week -1: dry-run on staging mirrors (no customer traffic).
- Day 0 (canary): 01:00–02:30 PT — 10% traffic to canary pool, 30m steady-state observation, then 1h gradual widen to 50% if healthy.
- Day 1 (rollout): 00:30–02:00 PT per pod; sequential pod rollout with 60m soak each.

Rollback triggers (examples):
- 30% increase in tail latency vs baseline for >15m.
- Production error rate spike (5xx) >0.5% sustained 10m.
- Data path failures (KV miss storm / cache corruption).

If those triggers fire, we revert to snapshot (T-10m) and re-route traffic to the previous binary for affected pods. Karthik, can you confirm the snapshot cadence and expected RTO for a full pod reversion?

If this sounds acceptable I'll circulate a single-page maintenance agreement for signature and open a short-lived Jira INF-2319 to track the work.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Staged upgrade: version curation, maintenance window proposal & reversion plan

Hi Priyom,

Thanks — reviewed quickly with our SREs. A couple of immediate constraints from our side:

1) Nightly blackout windows for our payments ledger run 01:00–01:45 PT daily; we cannot accept any disruptive changes inside that slot. Can you shift the canary earlier or later?
2) We require a documented audit trail for the snapshot/restore operations (who initiated, timeline). Is that part of your maintenance agreement?
3) For regulatory reasons we need to ensure that any rollback does not alter audit-immutable logs — is your revert process limited to runtime binaries and ephemeral data only?

Also, cost question from procurement — if we need a hotfix after the rollout that falls outside the agreed windows, will Redwood provide a grace patching credit or will that be billed at standard emergency rates? Please include pricing clarity in the maintenance agreement.

If you can update the timeline and include the audit controls, we can give a conditional go-ahead and assign an ops POC (I'll confirm the name by EOD).

Best,
Sylvia Ng
Head of Platform Ops
NovusBank

Subject: Re: Staged upgrade: version curation, maintenance window proposal & reversion plan

Sylvia / team — quick technical clarifications and commitments from our side:

Audit and immutability
- We will record all upgrade actions in the control plane with user and timestamp. The snapshot/restore steps operate on container images and ephemeral KV caches only. We will not rewrite append-only audit logs; reversion will point traffic back to the previous binary while preserving log files in place.

Snapshot cadence & expected RTO
- Snapshot frequency: we will take a filesystem + runtime metadata snapshot immediately prior to canary cut (T0) and again at T+30m during canary.
- RTO: single pod reversion to snapshot with traffic re-route tested internally is typically 6–9 minutes (includes image redeploy + cache warm). Full site reversion (all pods) worst-case 35–45 minutes.

Technical gating checklist (automated):
- healthcheck_ok across canary endpoints for 30m
- no 5xx increase above 0.5% sustained for 10m
- token throughput within 10% of baseline
- KV miss rate stable (no >2x baseline)

Network considerations
- We need ephemeral outbound to the Redwood package mirror for the canary (port 443 out). If your environment restricts that we can mirror artifacts into your private registry; let us know.

Emergency hotfix billing policy
- Marissa will follow up with procurement on preferred language, but standard practice: emergency out-of-window hotfixes are billable unless covered by a purchased emergency SLA addendum.

I will prepare an ops playbook snippet with exact CLI steps and the snapshot hash format we use so Novus' auditors can validate.

-Karthik
Engineering Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Sylvia — thanks for the quick feedback. Updated plan below addressing the blackout and audit asks: 

- Canary window moved to 23:00–00:30 PT (outside your payments ledger blackout). Full rollout per-pod windows shifted to 03:00–06:00 PT sequentially to minimize overlap with business hours.
- Audit: the maintenance_scope_summary.pdf now includes an audit checklist and a signed chain-of-custody stub. We will publish a signed event (control-plane entry) and provide the snapshot hashes to your audit team immediately after each snapshot.
- Billing: attached one-page proposal with emergency SLA options and costs. If Novus elects the Bronze emergency addendum we will cover one out-of-window hotpatch per 6-month period; otherwise standard emergency rates apply.

Next steps: if you confirm the updated windows and ops POC, I'll open Jira INF-2319 and create a one-click DocuSign for the maintenance agreement and emergency SLA addendum. Can you confirm POC and whether you want artifacts mirrored to your private registry?

I'll hold the bridge invite until I have POC names.

Regards,
Priyom Das
Senior Solutions Engineer
